task.description:
Step 3e — RIDE-ALONG, not rework. REVIEWER's Step 3d re-gate returned PASS (rework budget 1 of 3 used, 2 remaining) and raised four new MINOR findings, N1-N4, each a one-clause edit, explicitly recommending they ride along with the authorised backfill rather than spend a rework iteration. Read `handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03d-reviewer-regate.json`'s `result.issues` — each finding carries its measurement, its exact line numbers, and a proposed FIX, and N1 and N4 each carry a note about what the fix must NOT say. Follow those notes; they were written by an agent that had just measured the thing.

SIX ITEMS. The first four are REVIEWER's; the last two are this run's own findings and are the reason this step exists rather than the four being deferred.

(1) N1 — §3's stated derivation recipe does not reproduce §3's own table: running it literally yields 26 occurrences across 13 files, not 4, because the `orch_*` filter is stated semantically in the preceding sentence but is missing from the quoted procedure. The four rows and every cell are CORRECT; only the recipe is under-specified. This matters more than a normal typo because that paragraph exists to be re-derived and this run's entire subject is figures that did not survive re-derivation — the next agent who follows the instruction gets 26 and concludes the table is wrong. Apply REVIEWER's proposed clause.

(2) N2 — §4.1's 'Three such deaths are on record' is right for its class but states no class, and a sweep of the same window turns up a fourth abnormal termination (WF02-REQ025-20260817, `orchestrator.log:297`) that is genuinely OUTSIDE the class: the session that died was ORCH's own, between dispatches, holding no agent handoff, so no handoff `result` was ever left unwritten. Scope the sentence to 'deaths of a dispatched agent holding an open handoff', and add the WF02-REQ025 exclusion — REVIEWER's note is right that this is a useful boundary marker for the class, not merely a caveat.

(3) N3 — the date-scoped absence rule uses DAY granularity and its own day contains the counter-example it names. 43 handoffs created on 2026-08-21 predate commit 131aba9, and one of them is `handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json` — so the rule as written asserts, of that exact file, that its result is the acting agent's own report: the precise falsehood the field exists to prevent, about the one file the subsection singles out three paragraphs earlier. Scope the boundary to the landing COMMIT (`created on or after commit 131aba9`), which REVIEWER rates the most honest option and costs the same clause. Note that item (5) below closes the ISS-0109 half of this, but the other 42 files remain, so the commit-scoping is still required.

(4) N4 — §4.1(b)'s measurement paragraph never names the family it measures, under a heading that supplies a narrower one, so a reader entering at (b) can take the four instances as four reconstructions. Apply REVIEWER's clause. HEED ITS NOTE: the family is NOT 'ORCH writing a field it does not own' — that is wrong for WF02-REQ023, where ORCH corrected `created_at`/`started_at`, fields §3's table assigns to ORCH. The accurate framing is §3's own wording, 'a bookkeeping case the table did not cover'.

(5) PERFORM THE AUTHORISED BACKFILL on `handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json`. §4.1(b) names this file as the single exception to the no-backfill rule, and until it is done `grep -rl not_agent_attested handoffs/` — the command §4.1(b) offers as the field's entire justification — returns ZERO reconstructions in a repository containing exactly one. Rename its top-level `orch_reconstruction` key to `not_agent_attested` and add the one missing required member, `fields_written: ["status","completed_at","result"]`. The existing members map straight across (`reconstructed_by`, `reconstructed_at`, `reason`, `commands_run` → `evidence`, `not_verifiable_after_the_fact`) — check each against §4.1(b)'s table and rename `commands_run` to `evidence` only if §4.1(b) requires that member name; do not drop or reword any existing content. Add a short `backfill_note` member recording that this was a key rename performed by WF03-ISS0117-20260821 under §4.1(b)'s named exception, over evidence already present and already ORCH's own — NOT a retro-fitted claim. **This is a rename over existing evidence, never an authoring of new claims: you must not add, remove or reword a single factual assertion in that file.**

  MECHANICAL CONSTRAINT ON (5), non-negotiable: do NOT round-trip that file through `json.load`/`json.dump`. `docs/anti-patterns.md` documents a real incident where `json.dump`'s default `ensure_ascii=True` silently rewrote every non-ASCII character in a handoff file to a `\uXXXX` escape, changing ~1650 lines for a one-entry edit. Use a text edit on the raw JSON. Afterwards verify with a READ-ONLY `json.load` that the file still parses, and diff the parsed structure against the pre-edit one to confirm only the intended key rename and the two added members changed. Quote that verification.

(6) ADD AN ANTI-PATTERNS ENTRY to `docs/anti-patterns.md` for this run's most transferable finding, and give it a title naming the mechanism rather than the incident. THE FINDING: a wrong figure — 'five occurrences' — originated in the Step 1 diagnosis, passed through the Step 3 amendment, and then passed through REVIEWER's own Step 3b BLOCKER that was specifically correcting that very paragraph, because the gate re-derived the COUNT while inheriting the UNIT being counted. It was caught only at rework, when DOC-UPDATER stopped counting key names and read the four keys' VALUES, finding two of them were timestamp corrections in which no agent died. Three agents in sequence, each re-deriving diligently inside the wrong frame.

  WHY IT IS WORTH ITS OWN ENTRY rather than a line under the existing 'Inheriting a claim from a record' entry: this is the first recorded case where a GATE HANDOFF was the carrier. The existing entry's four instances are all a producer trusting a record; the correction mechanism assumed throughout is that a validator re-derives. Here the validator did re-derive, and still propagated the error, because re-deriving a number inside an inherited category is not re-derivation — it is a passing run of a different measurement, which is the same shape as core-directives.md's 'Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about'. Cross-link both. State the transferable rule plainly: when you re-derive a count, re-derive what is being counted, not only how many — and the cheap test that catches it, which is to read a sample of the underlying records' CONTENT rather than matching on the field name or key that defines the category.

  SECOND, SMALLER FINDING for the same entry or its own, your judgement: during this run REVIEWER replaced ORCH's ~6,300-character dispatched `task.description` in `step-03d-reviewer-regate.json` with a 156-character pointer reading 'See the PENDING copy of this handoff' — a copy that does not exist, since it is the same file. Because the file was untracked before that commit, the dispatched text existed in no git object and survived only in ORCH's own context, from which ORCH restored it verbatim. Do not overstate this: the run's verdict and evidence were unaffected. Its value is that it is a live instance of the exact gap §4.1 was written to close, in the field one row further along — which is item (7).

(7) ADD A `task` ROW TO §3's OWNERSHIP TABLE. §3's table now covers `created_at`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `status` and `result` — and still not `task`, which is the field the incident in (6) damaged. Add a row: `task` (and its `description`/`acceptance_criteria`), written by ORCH at handoff creation, never modified by the receiving agent; a receiving agent that believes its task block is wrong reports that in `result.issues` under §1.1 rather than editing it. Exception column: none. Cite the incident from (6) as the reason, in one clause, per the doc set's convention that every rule carries the incident that produced it. Keep it proportionate — this is a MINOR gap, not a second §4.1.

CONSTRAINTS. Write ONLY to the three files in `owned_modules`. Do NOT touch `docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md` (it passed the re-gate and needs nothing here), `core-directives.md`, any `docs/issues/*.yaml`, `handoffs/registry.json` or `handoffs/orchestrator.log`. Do NOT disturb anything the Step 3d re-gate PASSED — checks (A)-(G) all passed and no decision is reopened. No code, no tests. Do not call `gh` or the queue; report anything needing an id in `result.issues`.

RE-DERIVE, DO NOT INHERIT — and note that this instruction has now failed three times in this run, so treat it as the live hazard it is. Every figure you write must be measured in THIS pass, including any you take from REVIEWER's N1-N4 text. REVIEWER's findings are a record.
acceptance_criteria: N1, N2, N3 and N4 each fixed as specified, with N1's and N4's do-not-say notes honoured — in particular the family is described as 'a bookkeeping case §3's table did not cover', never as 'ORCH writing a field it does not own'
N3's boundary is scoped to commit 131aba9 (or an equivalent that excludes every pre-rule file), and no handoff created before the rule landed falls inside the absence-carries-attestation claim

The ISS-0109 backfill is performed: the file's top-level key is `not_agent_attested`, all six §4.1(b) members are present including `fields_written`, and a `backfill_note` records the rename, its authority, and that it was a rename over pre-existing evidence
No factual assertion in the ISS-0109 file was added, removed or reworded — verified by diffing the parsed structure before and after, with the verification quoted

The ISS-0109 file was edited as TEXT, not round-tripped through json.dump; it still parses under a read-only json.load, and its non-ASCII characters are unchanged — both confirmed by command and quoted
`grep -rl not_agent_attested handoffs/` now returns the ISS-0109 file — quote the command and its output, since making this command non-empty is the point of item (5)

docs/anti-patterns.md gains an entry whose title names the mechanism, which cross-links both 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' and core-directives.md's 'Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about', and which states the transferable rule and the cheap test that catches it
The anti-patterns entry is APPENDED; the file's existing entries are unchanged and its line count does not shrink — confirmed by command
§3's ownership table gains a `task` row citing the incident that produced it, proportionate in length to a MINOR gap
Every figure written in this pass was measured in this pass; result.summary names the commands that produced each
`git status --porcelain` shows changes confined to the three owned files plus this handoff; the output is quoted

result.summary:
All seven items applied. EVERY FIGURE BELOW WAS MEASURED IN THIS PASS; where my measurement disagreed with REVIEWER's N1-N4 text I wrote mine and say so. One item departs from REVIEWER's proposed clause on evidence -- see issue 1, it is the substantive finding of this step.

=== ITEM 5 FIRST, BECAUSE THE DOC TEXT CITES ITS RESULT: THE ISS-0109 BACKFILL ===
Edited as TEXT (two Edit calls on the raw JSON). NO json.dump round-trip at any point; the only json.load calls were read-only snapshots. Verification, quoted:
  Pre-edit snapshot: `python snap.py before.json` -> leaves: 63 | raw bytes: 13933 lines: 99 | non-ascii chars in raw: [] | md5 of raw: a4065ac771c8856f13f808ee6b981374
  Post-edit: `python snap.py after.json` -> leaves: 67 | raw bytes: 14756 lines: 105 | non-ascii chars in raw: [] | md5: d35d13c7eb1b7021f804266e28eefe20. The file still PARSES: json.load succeeded on it to produce that snapshot.
  PARSED-STRUCTURE DIFF (flattened leaf-path -> value maps, before vs after): 'REMOVED PATHS (14)' -- all 14 under /orch_reconstruction/. 'ADDED PATHS (18)' -- all 18 under /not_agent_attested/. 'CHANGED VALUES ON COMMON PATHS (0): []'. 'VALUES PRESENT BEFORE AND NOW GONE: []'. 'GENUINELY NEW VALUES (4)' -- the backfill_note string, plus 'status', 'completed_at', 'result' (the three fields_written entries). So: zero factual assertions added, removed or reworded; the 14 removed paths are the same 14 values under the renamed key and renamed member.
  NON-ASCII UNCHANGED: `grep -n -o '\\u[0-9a-fA-F]\{4\}'` -> exactly two matches, both on line 41 (\u26a0 \ufe0f), before and after. Literal non-ASCII characters: 0 before, 0 after. An ensure_ascii=False round-trip would have decoded those two escapes; it did not happen.
  MEMBER NAMES AND ORDER: `list(d['not_agent_attested'].keys())` -> ['reconstructed_by','reconstructed_at','reason','fields_written','evidence','not_verifiable_after_the_fact','backfill_note'] -- section 4.1(b)'s six in (b)'s exact order, with backfill_note appended 7th (see issue 2). `commands_run` was renamed to `evidence` because 4.1(b)'s table requires that member name. Top-level key order: not_agent_attested is 18th/18, matching section 2's fence.

    handoffs/orchestrator.log
    handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json

=== ITEM 6 -- ANTI-PATTERNS ENTRY (two entries; my judgement was that the smaller finding is a different mechanism and earns its own) ===
'## Re-deriving the count while inheriting the unit being counted' -- titled for the mechanism. Cross-links BOTH 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' and core-directives.md's 'Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about', and states why a gate carrying it is new. The four carriers were traced by reading the handoffs, not the run narrative: step-01-diagnose ('Five occurrences across four runs' while enumerating five run ids, one of which wrote no key), step-03-amendment ('THREE key names across FIVE occurrences' with a parenthetical listing four), step-03b-reviewer-gate (refuted 'five occurrences' -> four, then proposed 'five DEATH incidents across FIVE runs'), step-03c-rework1 (read the values, three deaths). The entry then records A FIFTH FIRING FOUND IN THIS PASS: step-03d re-derived the death count to three while inheriting the class boundary, and missed WF02-REQ038 -- whose dispatch committed nothing, so a sweep over handoff files structurally cannot see it. Transferable rule and the cheap test (read a sample of the underlying records' CONTENT rather than matching on the name/key/id that defines the category) are both stated.
  '## Overwriting a handoff's dispatched `task` block with a pointer to a copy that does not exist' -- the smaller finding, deliberately not overstated: it says in terms that the run's verdict and evidence were unaffected. Both character counts measured this pass: `git show 8f724cc:...step-03d-reviewer-regate.json` -> len(task.description) = 156, text 'See the PENDING copy of this handoff...'; working tree -> 6290.
  APPEND-ONLY CONFIRMED BY COMMAND: `git diff --numstat docs/anti-patterns.md` -> '102\t0' (102 insertions, ZERO deletions). Line count 968 -> 1070 (grew, did not shrink). `diff` of the two files' '^## ' heading lists -> '21a22,23' only: all 21 existing entry headings byte-identical, two appended.

One row (ORCH only / at handoff creation / exception: none), plus one proportionate paragraph citing the 6,290 -> 156 incident and pointing a disagreeing agent at result.issues per section 1.1. I also had to retitle the adjacent paragraph from 'Why the last two rows exist' to 'Why the `status` and `result` rows exist', since 'last two' would otherwise have silently re-pointed at the new row.

The rename made four existing sentences false. `grep -rn "orch_reconstruction" docs/` -> five sites, ALL inside HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (none in ORCHESTRATOR.md or core-directives.md, so nothing out of scope needed touching). issues.description: DEPARTURE FROM N2's PROPOSED CLAUSE, on measurement -- ORCH and REVIEWER should both see this. N2 proposed scoping the sentence to 'Three such deaths of a dispatched agent holding an open handoff'. Re-deriving in this pass, that scoped sentence is FALSE: there are FOUR. WF02-REQ038-20260817's run entry in handoffs/registry.json (line 729) records 'One infra-terminated CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR dispatch (connection error mid-work, zero commits, cleanly re-dispatched from scratch without incrementing rework_count -- matching the WF02-REQ027-20260816 step_2d_infra_restart precedent)'. That is a dispatched agent, holding an open handoff, dying mid-work -- section 4.1's class exactly, and the same treatment as the WF02-REQ027 row already in the table. So I added a fourth row rather than applying N2's clause literally, and the prose now reads 'Four incidents, three different treatments'. WHY IT WAS MISSED BY THE STEP 3D SWEEP, which did have the line in its grep output: the incident left no handoff file and no orchestrator.log line, because the dead dispatch committed nothing -- it exists only as one clause inside a run-level note, so it does not look like a death record, it looks like prose. THIS IS BEYOND THE ONE-CLAUSE MINOR I WAS DISPATCHED TO APPLY: it changes a table and a headline figure that PASSED the Step 3d re-gate, and the four-row table has not been through any gate. The argument of 4.1 is unaffected (the two redispatches are one treatment, so 'three different treatments, one of which was no treatment at all' still holds). ORCH's call whether this warrants a REVIEWER look; I judged that shipping a figure I had measured as wrong would be the exact failure this run exists to document.

NEEDS AN ID. Section 4.1(b) says not_agent_attested is 'an object with all six members below', and the backfilled ISS-0109 file now carries SEVEN -- the six, plus the `backfill_note` my dispatch required. By the letter, 'all six' is a floor and not a closed set, so the file complies; but (b) is written as a schema and a linter built from it would plausibly reject an unlisted member. Either (b) gains a one-clause allowance ('additional members are permitted only to record the provenance of a rename authorised under this subsection') or the note moves somewhere else. I did not edit (b)'s member table myself: that is a schema decision, and the re-gate passed (b) as it stands.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT MINE, LEFT UNTOUCHED, AND STILL UNCOMMITTED. handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03d-reviewer-regate.json was already dirty in the working tree when this step began -- `git diff --numstat` shows 8 insertions / 8 deletions, which is ORCH's verbatim restoration of the 6,290-character task.description that the completing agent had replaced with a 156-character pointer. It is outside my owned_modules so I did not stage or commit it, and it is NOT in my commit. It needs to be committed by ORCH, and until it is, the restored dispatch text still exists in no git object -- which is the same exposure the incident itself created.

THREE OF REVIEWER's N1/N3 SUB-FIGURES DID NOT REPRODUCE, all small, all now carrying my measurements in the doc. (a) N1: top-level `next_action` appears in SIX files, not five -- N1's own enumeration lists six while saying five. (b) N3: 46 handoffs carry a created_at on 2026-08-21, not 45 -- the extra is this step's own handoff, created after N3 was written, so N3 was right when written. (c) N3: 42 of them predate commit 131aba9, not 43 -- the difference is step-03b-reviewer-gate.json at 07:13:55Z, 47 seconds AFTER the commit's 07:13:08Z; comparing created_at strings against the commit's LOCAL-time stamp (12:13:08+05:00) rather than its UTC instant would misplace exactly that file. Reported rather than filed: (b) is not an error at all, and (a)/(c) change no conclusion. Noting them because this run's subject is figures that did not survive re-derivation, and these did not.
